title: Average, highest and lowest GPA
prompt_md:
The **Students** sheet holds 120 students; GPAs are in column **F** (rows 2–121).

On the **Answers** sheet, put formulas in:

- `B2` — the average GPA
- `B3` — the highest GPA
- `B4` — the lowest GPA

Answer cells must contain formulas, not typed numbers.

example.input_md: `=AVERAGE(Students!F2:F121)` is the shape of the first answer.

hints: `AVERAGE`, `MAX` and `MIN` all take a range: `Students!F2:F121`.
Click a cell, type `=`, then click/drag on the Students sheet (or type the range) and press Enter.

title: Counting things
prompt_md:
On the **Answers** sheet:

- `B2` — how many students are on the Students sheet (count the ids in `A2:A121`)
- `B3` — how many students have **no advisor** (blank cells in `Students!G2:G121`)
- `B4` — how many courses are on the Courses sheet (numeric ids in `Courses!A2:A137`)

example.input_md: `COUNTA` counts non-empty cells, `COUNT` counts numbers, `COUNTBLANK` counts empty cells.

hints: `=COUNTA(Students!A2:A121)`
`=COUNTBLANK(Students!G2:G121)` and `=COUNT(Courses!A2:A137)`

title: Honors flag with IF
prompt_md:
On the **Students** sheet, column **I** has the header `honors`. Fill `I2:I121` with a formula that shows `Honors` when the student's GPA (column F) is **3.5 or higher**, and an empty string `""` otherwise.

Write the formula once in `I2`, then select `I2:I121` and use **Fill down** (or Ctrl+D).

example.input_md: `=IF(F2>=3.5,"Honors","")` in I2, then fill down — relative references adjust row by row.

hints: `IF(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false)`
Select I2, shift-click I121, press Ctrl+D.
oracle: cells = fill('Students', 'I', lambda r: 'Honors' if r.gpa >= 3.5 else '')

title: Short names with text functions
prompt_md:
On the **Students** sheet, column **J** has the header `short_name`. Fill `J2:J121` with the student's first initial, a period, a space and the last name — e.g. `Miguel Bennett` → `M. Bennett`.

Use `LEFT`, `UPPER` and `CONCATENATE` (or the `&` operator). Note: this engine has no `CONCAT`.
hints: `LEFT(text, 1)` takes the first character.
`CONCATENATE(a, b, c)` or `a & b & c` joins strings.
oracle: cells = fill('Students', 'J', lambda r: r.first_name[0].upper() + '. ' + r.last_name)

title: Faculty payroll
prompt_md:
The **Employees** sheet lists 100 faculty with salaries in column **F** (rows 2–101).

On **Answers**: `B2` = total payroll, `B3` = average salary, `B4` = highest salary.
hints: `SUM`, `AVERAGE`, `MAX` over `Employees!F2:F101`.
Cross-sheet references look like `SheetName!A1:B9`.
oracle: E = X['Employees']; cells = [['Answers!B2', int(E.salary.sum())], ['Answers!B3', E.salary.mean()], ['Answers!B4', int(E.salary.max())]]

title: Conditional aggregates
prompt_md:
On **Answers**:

- `B2` — number of students from **MO** with GPA **≥ 3.5** (Students: state in column D, GPA in F)
- `B3` — total salary of employees in **department 1** (Employees: department_id in column E, salary in F)
- `B4` — average GPA of students from **IL**

This engine has `AVERAGEIF` but **not** `AVERAGEIFS`.
hints: Criteria with comparison operators are strings: `">=3.5"`.
`=SUMIFS(sum_range, criteria_range, criteria)` and `=AVERAGEIF(range, criteria, average_range)`.
oracle: S = X['Students']; E = X['Employees']; cells = [['Answers!B2', int(((S.home_state == 'MO') & (S.gpa >= 3.5)).sum())], ['Answers!B3', int(E[E.department_id == 1].salary.sum())], ['Answers!B4', S[S.home_state == 'IL'].gpa.mean()]]

title: Look up the course with VLOOKUP
prompt_md:
Each row of **Enrollments** has a `section_id` in column **C**. The **Sections** sheet maps `section_id` (column A) to `course_id` (column B).

Column **H** of Enrollments has the header `course_id`. Fill `H2:H301` with the course id of each enrollment's section using `VLOOKUP` with an exact match. Lock the lookup table with `$` so it survives fill-down.
hints: `VLOOKUP(lookup_value, table, column_index, FALSE)` — the 4th argument FALSE means exact match.
Use `$A$2:$E$237` so the table does not shift when you fill down.
oracle: sec = X['Sections'].set_index('section_id').course_id; cells = fill('Enrollments', 'H', lambda r: int(sec[r.section_id]))

title: INDEX / MATCH for course titles
prompt_md:
On the **Sections** sheet, column **F** has the header `course_title`. Fill `F2:F237` with the title of each section's course (`course_id` in column B). The **Courses** sheet has `course_id` in column A and `title` in column D.

Use `INDEX` + `MATCH` (not VLOOKUP).
hints: `MATCH(value, one_column_range, 0)` returns the row position; `INDEX(range, position)` reads it.
Lock both ranges with `$`.
oracle: t = X['Courses'].set_index('course_id').title; cells = fill('Sections', 'F', lambda r: t[r.course_id])

title: Letter bands with IFS
prompt_md:
On **Students**, column **K** has the header `band`. Fill `K2:K121` with a letter based on GPA (column F):

| GPA | band |
|---|---|
| ≥ 3.7 | A |
| ≥ 3.3 | B |
| ≥ 3.0 | C |
| otherwise | D |

Use `IFS` or nested `IF`s.
hints: Conditions are evaluated top to bottom; order them from the highest threshold down.
The final `TRUE,"D"` pair is the catch-all.
oracle: cells = fill('Students', 'K', lambda r: 'A' if r.gpa >= 3.7 else 'B' if r.gpa >= 3.3 else 'C' if r.gpa >= 3.0 else 'D')

title: Dates and IFERROR
prompt_md:
**Employees** has `hire_date` in column **G** (real dates). Column **H** has the header `hire_year`.

1. Fill `H2:H101` with the hire year (`YEAR`).
2. `Answers!B2` — the number of **complete years** between the earliest hire date and 1 January 2025 (`DATEDIF(start, DATE(2025,1,1), "Y")`).
3. `Answers!B3` — look up the course id for section **99999** on the Sections sheet with VLOOKUP, but show the text `not found` instead of an error (`IFERROR`).
hints: `YEAR(G2)`; `MIN` of a date column gives the earliest date.
`=IFERROR(VLOOKUP(99999,Sections!A2:E237,2,FALSE),"not found")`
oracle: E = X['Employees']; cells = fill('Employees', 'H', lambda r: int(r.hire_date[:4])) + [['Answers!B2', datedif_y(E.hire_date.min(), '2025-01-01')], ['Answers!B3', 'not found']]

title: Two-way INDEX / MATCH
prompt_md:
The **Answers** sheet has a `course_id` in column A and an `attribute` name (one of the Courses headers: `credits`, `level`, `title`, …) in column B for rows 2–4.

Fill `C2:C4` with a **single formula pattern** that looks up the row by course id **and** the column by header name: `INDEX(table, MATCH(id, id_column, 0), MATCH(attribute, header_row, 0))`. Include row 1 of Courses in the table so the header row lines up.
hints: The second MATCH searches the header row `Courses!A1:F1` for the attribute name.
Both MATCHes must use the same starting row as the INDEX table.
oracle: C = X['Courses'].set_index('course_id'); v = lambda i, a: C.loc[i, a]; cells = [['Answers!C2', int(v(50, 'credits'))], ['Answers!C3', int(v(77, 'level'))], ['Answers!C4', v(12, 'title')]]

title: SUMPRODUCT with several criteria
prompt_md:
`SUMPRODUCT` multiplies arrays element-wise and sums the result; a comparison like `(range="MO")` is an array of 1/0, so multiplying comparisons ANDs them.

On **Answers**:

- `B2` — number of **completed** enrollments (Enrollments column E) with grade points (column G) **≥ 3.7**
- `B3` — the **sum of GPAs** of students from **MO** who enrolled in **2023** (Students D, E, F)
- `B4` — the **average GPA** of students from **IL** who enrolled in **2022** (a SUMPRODUCT divided by a SUMPRODUCT)
hints: Wrap each comparison in parentheses and multiply: `(A)*(B)*values`.
For the average: `SUMPRODUCT((cond1)*(cond2)*F)/SUMPRODUCT((cond1)*(cond2))`.

answers: Sum of GPAs: MO students enrolled 2023

oracle: S = X['Students']; En = X['Enrollments']; il22 = S[(S.home_state == 'IL') & (S.enrollment_year == 2022)]; cells = [['Answers!B2', int(((En.status == 'completed') & (En.grade_points >= 3.7)).sum())], ['Answers!B3', float(S[(S.home_state == 'MO') & (S.enrollment_year == 2023)].gpa.sum())], ['Answers!B4', il22.gpa.mean()]]

title: Nth largest / smallest with a condition
prompt_md:
`LARGE(IF(condition, values), n)` evaluates `IF` over whole ranges (array arithmetic is enabled in this workbook) and keeps only the values where the condition holds.

On **Answers**:

- `B2` — the **2nd highest** salary in department **1** (Employees: department in E, salary in F)
- `B3` — the **3rd lowest** GPA among students from **MO** (Students: state D, GPA F)
- `B4` — the highest salary among employees whose title is exactly `Assistant Professor` (`MAXIFS` or `MAX(IF(...))`)
hints: Inside `IF`, compare a whole range with a value: `Employees!E2:E101=1`.
`=MAXIFS(Employees!F2:F101,Employees!D2:D101,"Assistant Professor")`
oracle: S = X['Students']; E = X['Employees']; cells = [['Answers!B2', int(E[E.department_id == 1].salary.sort_values(ascending=False).iloc[1])], ['Answers!B3', float(S[S.home_state == 'MO'].gpa.sort_values().iloc[2])], ['Answers!B4', int(E[E.title == 'Assistant Professor'].salary.max())]]

title: Department of each enrollment (three-sheet lookup)
prompt_md:
Column **I** of **Enrollments** has the header `department`. Fill `I2:I301` with the **name of the department** that owns the course of each enrollment's section.

The chain is: `Enrollments.section_id` (C) → `Sections.course_id` (B) → `Courses.department_id` (B) → `Departments.name` (C). Nest the lookups in one formula.
hints: Build it inside-out: first the course id (VLOOKUP into Sections), then the department id (INDEX/MATCH into Courses), then the name (INDEX/MATCH into Departments).
Test each layer in a spare cell before nesting.
oracle: sec = X['Sections'].set_index('section_id').course_id; cdep = X['Courses'].set_index('course_id').department_id; dn = X['Departments'].set_index('department_id').name; cells = fill('Enrollments', 'I', lambda r: dn[cdep[sec[r.section_id]]])

title: Per-student average grade points
prompt_md:
Column **L** of **Students** has the header `avg_grade_points`. For each student (id in column A), fill `L2:L121` with the **average of `grade_points`** over that student's rows on the Enrollments sheet (student_id in B, grade_points in G).

Students with **no** enrollment rows on the sheet must show an empty string `""` (guard with `IF(COUNTIF(...)=0, "", ...)`). Use SUMPRODUCT and COUNTIF with locked ranges.
hints: `SUMPRODUCT((Enrollments!$B$2:$B$301=A2)*Enrollments!$G$2:$G$301)` sums the grade points of one student.
Divide by `COUNTIF(Enrollments!$B$2:$B$301,A2)`; wrap in `IF(COUNTIF(...)=0,"",...)`.
oracle: g = X['Enrollments'].groupby('student_id').grade_points.mean(); cells = fill('Students', 'L', lambda r: float(g[r.student_id]) if r.student_id in g.index else '')
